Pooled: whole_piece 17/17 (100%); claim_level 75/88 (85%); tautological 10/10 (100%); check-case pairs not evaluable from letter text: 86.

How to read this:
- **claim_level** (lexical/structural triggers on the claim itself) is the informative number.
- **whole_piece** checks (risk present, established name, MedWatch, etc.) are run on letter *excerpts*; a hit is only semi-informative because the letter already tells us the element was absent.
- **tautological** (`form_2253`): the fixture encodes the letter's finding, so 100% is by construction. Reported, not counted.
- Not evaluable: dual modality, super legibility/reading speed, audio pacing, risk-after-close, risk coverage (need the asset or a full PI risk list).
- **Circularity caveat:** the checks and lexicons were written while looking at these same letters; there is no held-out split. Treat recall as an upper bound on in-distribution recall, not a generalization estimate.

Trigger checks are designed to route text to a human or a substantiation lookup, so a fire on compliant text costs review time; it is not an approval error. Tuning between v0 and now (all generic, none case-specific): negation handling ('not cured', 'no studies have shown ... safer'), placebo/vehicle/baseline comparators no longer count as comparative claims, 'only' requires an exclusivity construction ('the only', 'only FDA-approved'), the investigational-code regex no longer matches 'FDA-2253', '50 x 10^9/L' is not a relative multiplier, risk-link labels ('View Important Safety Info') no longer count as risk content, empty-text fixtures return needs_input. The v0→v1 change cost one recall hit: exclusivity_claim lost the 'another ... option' pattern. Because tuning used these controls, the after-tuning FP numbers are optimistic.

Whole-piece checks (MedWatch, adequate provision, cost info, Rx indicator, established name, risk present, etc.) fire on most controls because controls are claim excerpts, not complete pieces; those rates are not FP estimates and are omitted here (raw numbers in `det_results.json`).

## 4. Pairwise set

`evals/pairwise.jsonl`: 207 items: 156 easy (letter-quoted original vs synthetic rewrite) + 51 near-miss (hand-authored, fictional products, one subtle difference each). A/B order seeded-random (expected winner A=100, B=107). Each item carries one rule question with pass/fail anchors from the rulebook, `expected_winner`, and `expected_approvable` per side (the violating side is always false; the compliant side is true for near-misses and unknown (null) for easy pairs, since rewrites contain [placeholders]). 156 of 176 controls became pairs; omitted: originals that are only the letter's description of an omission/process (no piece text to compare).

Easy pairs are easier than Crosby's agent-draft vs lawyer-final pairs (the original is a known violation and the rewrite often contains bracketed placeholders), so they only set a floor: a judge that can't win these isn't ready.

## 5. Judge

Prompts: `judge/pairwise_prompt.md`, `judge/single_prompt.md`. Runner: `judge/run_judge.py` (OpenRouter by default; responses cached in `judge/results/cache.jsonl`; $3 spend cap). Raw verdicts: `judge/results/raw.jsonl`.

**Model:** `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` via OpenRouter (paid; listed price $0.1/M input, $0.5/M output). **Cost:** $0.3762 total across all judge runs (OpenRouter-reported per-call cost, summed from the response cache; by model: {'nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free': 0.0, 'anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5': 0.3762}); last run $0.0000 for 0 new calls + 732 cache hits. Last run finished 2026-10-07T22:53:28-07:00. Note: Free attempt first: nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free passed the 5/5 probe and a 12-call smoke run, then throughput collapsed to ~1 call/min under OpenRouter free-tier limits (429 'free-models-per-min', limit 20/min). Killed after ~79 cached answers; full run redone on a cheap paid fallback (first model in the runner paid-preference list, under $1/M input, that passed the probe) so all verdicts come from one model. Rerun after lenient-parser fix: only previously unparseable answers were re-requested. v2 rerun after fixing item/prompt defects found in v1 failure review (see report). Model selection: the runner probes free models first (5 real pairwise prompts; needs >=4 parseable answers); see the note above for which model was used and why.

Every pair was judged in both A/B orders (original order and swapped), so each pair contributes 2 verdicts.

### Single-item 'would you sign off on this rule as is' judging

- Near-miss violating versions judged FAIL: 26/27 (96%); near-miss compliant versions judged PASS: 23/27 (85%).
- Easy pairs: letter-cited originals judged FAIL: 142/155 (92%); synthetic rewrites judged PASS: 89/155 (57%) (rewrites contain [placeholders] and visual notes, so a FAIL/missing-context there is often reasonable).
- Judge set missing_context=true on 123 single-item verdicts; unparseable/errored: 2.

### Pairwise failures, read and characterized

1 wrong pairwise verdicts. Categories: bad_rewrite = our 'compliant' side isn't actually better on this rule; judge_error = judge misread or missed the decisive difference; ambiguous_item = rule question/label facts underdetermine the answer; position = wrong only in one order.

- [calibrate] PW-UL-20260622-193307-v3 (A-202-E6-04J, orig): judge reason: "Neither version mentions the PI limitation that PDT is not suitable for esophageal ulcers >1 cm, so both omit a labeled risk. Version B's unqualified 'selectively destroys the cancer cells' implies tissue-sparing safety " → **bad_rewrite (+position)**. The LLM-drafted 'compliant' rewrite only dropped 'with a diameter of up to 1.2cm' and kept 'selectively destroys the cancer cells', and the pair was assigned a minimization rule (A-202-E6-04J) for what is really an efficacy/mechanism problem. The judge's reasoning (the unqualified version implies more tissue-sparing safety) is defensible. It got the swapped order right, so this is also a position-sensitive call.

Failure categories: bad_rewrite (+position) 1

### Single-item near-miss failures, read and characterized

- PW-NM-12 (A-202-E2-01, compliant side judged fail): "The piece names the product and its indication (major depressive disorder), so it cannot qualify as a reminder ad under 202.1(e)(2)(i), which forbids indications in reminder ads. It also presents as a" → **ambiguous_item (rule text gap)**. Rule A-202-E2-01's text covers reminder-ad content (no indication or dosage) but omits the 202.1(e)(2)(i) bar on reminder ads for boxed-warning drugs, which is what the item tests. The judge applied the rule text correctly on both sides. Fix the rule text, not the judge.
- PW-NM-12 (A-202-E2-01, violating side judged pass): "The piece names the product and strength but states no indication (depression is not mentioned) and gives no dosage recommendation, so this specific requirement is met on its face. The label's boxed w" → **ambiguous_item (rule text gap)**. Rule A-202-E2-01's text covers reminder-ad content (no indication or dosage) but omits the 202.1(e)(2)(i) bar on reminder ads for boxed-warning drugs, which is what the item tests. The judge applied the rule text correctly on both sides. Fix the rule text, not the judge.
- PW-NM-13 (B-SM-01, compliant side judged fail): "The piece presents serious risks (anaphylaxis, not for acute bronchospasm) but contains no benefit information, so risk is not presented together with benefit within this character-limited communicati" → **judge_error**. The compliant sponsored link states the indication plus the serious risks. The judge failed it for having 'no benefit information', which misreads the rule: risk is required when benefits are claimed, and benefits aren't required.
- PW-NM-21 (A-202-E6-09, compliant side judged fail): "The piece makes a specific guideline preference claim (NCCN-recommended) but cites no guideline, reference, or recommendation category, so nothing in the text supports the claim. The requirement that " → **ambiguous_item**. The compliant side claims 'NCCN-recommended option in that setting' without naming a version or category. The judge wanted the citation specified, which is a reasonable strict reading. The item should include the guideline version.
- PW-NM-25 (D-SP-03, compliant side judged fail): "The label facts say the same program content repeats monthly, yet the log records only a first attendance and does not flag repeat attendance or screen attendees for business reason as suspect. The pi" → **judge_error**. An attendance log showing first attendance does meet the repeat-attendance criterion. The judge wanted the log itself to screen for repeat attendance, which is over-strict.

Easy originals judged PASS (13; 10 of them flagged missing_context): mostly an **item-rule mismatch**. `make_pairwise.py` assigns each easy pair the first judgment rule linked to its case, so emotional taglines or visual-only problems get asked a data-support question (B-CFL-03, A-202-E5-01), and the quoted excerpt alone doesn't trigger it. Two are judge leniency: Recorlev's 'will help your doctor avoid side effects' passed under a lexicon-style minimization rule, and Gvoke's 'Easy to know you did it right' passed under an efficacy rule. Fix: give each easy pair the rule that matches the letter's category.

Easy rewrites judged FAIL: 66 (missing_context on most). Expected, because rewrites carry [placeholders]; this is not a judge error signal.

Empty output: the model returned no content for every call on PW-UL-20250909-188902-v2 (Jeuveau botulinum-toxin newsletter, 4 calls). Likely provider-side safety filtering; those calls are excluded from accuracy.

### v1 → v2 (fixes made after reading v1 failures; disclosed because they were made after seeing results)

- v1: calibration 308/310 (99%); near-miss pairwise 54/54 (100%); single near-miss violating→FAIL 27/27 (100%), compliant→PASS 21/27 (78%).
- Fixes: (1) deterministic-rule anchors no longer paste the check's metadata logic. In v1 the judge failed compliant text because 'meta.substantiated_claims' / 'meta.reference_checks' were absent (NM-15, NM-21). (2) Two near-miss pairs were mapped to the wrong OIG rule (NM-24 venue/alcohol → D-SP-01, was D-SP-03; NM-25 repeat attendance → D-SP-03, was D-SP-04). (3) NM-23's compliant payor side lacked the material-differences statement the rule requires, so it was added (to both sides' indication framing too, so only the disclosures differ). (4) A lenient JSON parser now handles answers with unescaped quotes inside 'reason' (13 v1 calibration answers were unparseable).
- v2 (headline numbers above): calibration 309/310 (100%); near-miss pairwise 54/54 (100%); single near-miss violating→FAIL 26/27 (96%), compliant→PASS 23/27 (85%).

## 7. Gaps

- **Judge:** one model (claude-haiku-5.5; v1 run, then v2 after item/prompt fixes), no human agreement baseline; calibration pairs are easy by construction, so the near-miss and single-item numbers matter more. The 82 LLM-drafted controls came from an xAI model and the judge is an Anthropic model, so the judge is not grading its own rewrites. The judge model was chosen because the free model was rate-limited, not because it was evaluated as best.
- **No human labels.** Controls (82 LLM-drafted, 94 agent-authored) and near-miss pairs are unreviewed by a regulatory reviewer. Crosby's method hinges on expert comparisons; this set is a scaffold until the owner's MLR team reviews it. At least one LLM control (Vyepti post hoc) is not actually compliant.
- **Circularity:** checks were tuned while viewing these letters and controls; no held-out split. Next step: freeze checks and score on letters issued after 2026-10-07, or hold out a random 30% of letters.
- **Visual/audiovisual cases** (distraction, dual modality, super legibility, pacing, airtime): checks exist but need asset metadata (supers, timings, wpm); letters can't supply it, so they're not evaluable here. Needs real assets from PromoMats.
- **Risk coverage** (37 linked cases) needs a structured PI risk list per product; none loaded. This is the biggest deterministic blind spot.
- **Sources not fetched/verified:** 21 CFR 314.81 text (cited as letters cite it); Brief Summary 2015 draft quote unchecked against source; revised 'Addressing Misinformation' draft (supersedes 2014) and the June 2026 payor Q&A draft revision not fetched; ACCME Standards, GPP 2022, HIPAA patient-story authorization not done; ex-US codes (EFPIA, ABPI, PMCPA, IFPMA) skipped by instruction.
- **FTC/OIG/PhRMA rules** have no real positives (OPDP letters don't cite them). Need FTC actions (e.g., health-claim cases), OIG/DOJ speaker-program settlements and CIA reports as positive sources.
- **Easy pairs are easy:** originals are known violations and rewrites contain [placeholders]. Near-miss pairs (51) are the meaningful judge test, but there are few and they cover only 48 rules.
